payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the edited image show any change to the mug’s position relative to the headphones?
node.criteria: pass: The mug’s position relative to the headphones visibly changed. fail: The mug’s position relative to the headphones visibly did not change. unknown: A change cannot be determined from the available images.
node.binding: Compare the original and edited images only to assess progress toward the requested relative-position change; unrelated edits do not count.

node_traces.evidence: The mug’s position relative to the headphones visibly changed between the source and edited images; the edited image shows a mug on the headphones’ right, indicating progress toward the requested move.

fulfillment: The node’s binding is too vague (“mug (...) right of the headphones”) and its trace treats the final spatial relation as sufficient for completion. In the supplied images, the source has one blue mug left of the headphones, while the edit appears to contain multiple mugs and a blue blur at the original location; the rightmost mug is not clearly the original target. Do not infer completion or progress merely from a mug appearing on the right or from a reported positional change. Bind the requested mug across source and edit using visual identity and compare its location relative to the headphones; assess whether the evidence establishes that the target itself moved, whether the requested relation is complete, and whether any apparent change is instead duplication, replacement, or ambiguous. Preserve unknown when identity or movement cannot be established. The high-confidence yes trace conflicts with the partial reference, but the label is aggregate guidance, not atomic ground truth; investigate this binding/evidence gap rather than forcing partial. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated.

response.content: {"text":"Improve the binding so it tracks the specific source mug (the large blue mug left of the headphones) across the edit, rather than treating any mug on the right or any changed spatial relation as evidence of progress. The edited image appears to show a blue blur at the source location and two smaller mugs, so the target’s identity and whether it was moved, replaced, or duplicated are uncertain. Make the check distinguish evidence that the original target itself moved from mere presence of another mug to the right, and assess progress separately from whether the requested final relation is complete. Use unknown when the images do not establish target identity or movement; do not force a label from the aggregate reference. The high-confidence pass conflicts with the partial aggregate, so investigate this evidence/binding gap and calibrate confidence to the ambiguity. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated."}
